goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate says that several goroutines can build the same index for the same key at once. C3 does note that cacheMu no longer covers BuildIndex, but only to explain the TotalDocs map race, not duplicate index builds.

goldens.comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
goldens.reasoning: C3 describes the same problem: TotalDocs loops over b.cache without a lock while the watcher goroutine's BuildIndex writes to it, which can cause a concurrent map access panic.

candidates: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35 - The storage-server integration test is now skipped on Postgres instead of fixed.. When `GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres`, this test now skips. That is the CI configuration where it was failing, so the startup path this PR changes (`Init` now runs inside `NewResourceServer`) is no longer tested on Postgres. The PR summary calls this "Enhanced PostgreSQL integration test compatibility", but the change turns the test off. Fix the Postgres failure, or at least link a tracking issue and make sure the test still runs in another CI job.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 - Removing `Init` from every handler means `Stop` no longer blocks requests.. `Stop` sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"`. That only rejected requests because each handler (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned `initErr`. With those calls gone, requests that arrive after `Stop` keep going to a backend that has been cancelled, and `IsHealthy` keeps reporting SERVING during shutdown. Add a cheap check for `s.initErr` (or a stopping flag) at the top of the handlers, or at least in `IsHealthy`.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 - The new `TotalDocs` call reads the index cache map while the watcher may be writing to it.. The event goroutine started just above can call `handleEvent` → `getOrCreateIndex` → `BuildIndex`, which writes `b.cache[key]`. `TotalDocs` loops over `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`. If an event arrives right after init and creates a new index, Go can crash with "concurrent map iteration and map write". This PR also stops holding `cacheMu` around `BuildIndex`, so nothing serializes the two any more. Take `cacheMu` (or a read lock) inside `TotalDocs`, or log before starting the watcher goroutine.
